summary.text: A 33-year-old gravida four, para two woman self-detected a left axillary mass at 17 weeks of pregnancy. There was no definite immediate family history of breast or ovarian cancer and BRCA mutation testing was negative. Ultrasound and mammography showed an axillary mass with microcalcifications, while staging chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were unremarkable.

Ultrasound-guided biopsy showed a high-grade carcinoma consistent with a breast primary that was ER, PR and HER-2 negative. After informed discussion she had a left mastectomy at 20 weeks’ gestation, with histology of a 9 mm grade 3, receptor-negative, node-positive (4/17 nodes) invasive ductal carcinoma, pT1b pN2a.

Adjuvant chemotherapy was three cycles of FEC every 3 weeks followed by weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m^(2), paused after six paclitaxel cycles at 36 weeks’ gestation for Caesarean delivery at 38 weeks and 6 days of an infant weighing 3700 g. Chemotherapy recommenced 2 weeks after delivery with bottle feeding, and milk was expressed and discarded. Radiotherapy followed chemotherapy; hormonal therapy was not recommended.

Plasma and breast milk samples were taken after the 9th week of weekly paclitaxel. Plasma peaked at 2050 ng/mL 1 h after chemotherapy, breast milk peaked 2.75 h after chemotherapy, and milk levels were below the minimum quantifiable concentration by 71.25 h. Relative infant dose was 0.247% at 27 h and at most 0.091% at 72 h.

article_limitations: Figures 1 to 3 plot the same concentrations printed in Table 1; plot points are not read, only printed table values and text values are recorded.

The relative infant dose uses a population 50th centile infant weight estimate, not a measured infant weight, and a standard daily milk volume of 150 mL/kg per the formula; the formula image has no resolved asset.
Table 1 time labels and the text sampling times differ in places (2.75 h versus 3 h, plasma 6.5 and 8.5 h not tabulated, a 193 h row not in the text list); see ambiguities.
Time of each concentration is the Table 1 row label in hours; the table does not state the reference point, and the Results/abstract state hours following chemotherapy for some values only.
Table cells that are blank (plasma after 6 h, milk before 3 h) are not reported and are not recorded as zero or missing results.
Whether the sampled dose was the 9th weekly dose, and the number of paclitaxel cycles delivered after the pause, are not stated explicitly.

The abstract and Results give 72 h as the time of the maximum relative infant dose; the milk samples at 71.25 and 75.75 h are below the minimum quantifiable concentration and 72 h is not a listed sampling time.
